messages:
maria: :rotating_light: sec-scan flagged a probable customer API token inside a frontend error payload that was uploaded to Sentry a few minutes ago. link: https://sentry.redwood/example/issue/12345
sec-bot: Automated scan (secret-scan v2) detected pattern: ^cus_[A-Za-z0-9-_]{24} in event payload path 'event.context.extra.reported_error'. confidence: high.
sam: yikes — that payload came from the error-reporting form on /embed. I can pull the event.
raj: can we confirm which key and whether it's a customer-managed key vs our internal ingest key? priority: P0 until we know.
maria: initial lookup: value starts with "cus_" which matches customer API keys. Appears tied to customer_id=8392 in the same payload. No evidence yet it's one of our service keys.
toni: reaching out to CSM for customer 8392 to notify and ask if they've rotated recently. I'll draft a cautious message.
sam: grabbing full event now. snippet: ```json
{
  "user": {"id":"u-792"},
  "customer_id":8392,
  "error": "TypeError...",
  "extra": {"reportText":"...","apiKey":"cus_3hG7...zQp"}
}
```
raj: OK next steps: 1) verify if that token is valid (call internal token-validate) 2) check audit logs for recent usage 3) if valid, rotate/invalidate ASAP and notify customer. Assigning to infra oncall.
maria: raj, can you run `tokenctl validate cus_3hG7...zQp` and `auditlogs query --key cus_3hG7...zQp --last 7d`?
raj: running now. results: `tokenctl` -> VALID, last use 2026-03-20T09:12:04 UTC from ip 54.23.11.9 hitting /v1/embeds. `auditlogs` -> 3 successful requests in the last 2 hours from two distinct IPs: 54.23.11.9 and 34.201.2.4.
sam: that IP range looks like a customer host (checked reverse DNS). Could be legitimate but still sensitive.
maria: treat as compromise until proven otherwise. Sam — can you identify whether frontend ever logs full API keys? we should fix that code path.
sam: yes, it's a bug in the error reporter that serializes full request body. opening PR to sanitize now: https://github.com/redwood/embed-frontend/pull/425
raj: containment: I recommend immediate invalidation of that key, generate replacement for customer, and run a replay detection job to enumerate suspicious API calls from the last 24h. I'll coordinate with infra.
maria: before invalidating, Toni please confirm customer impact window and agree on comms. Toni: we should offer rotation, confirm whether they saw unexpected usage first.
toni: on it. DMing user contact + opening a customer incident. Draft message: "We detected that an API key for your account may have been included in an error report. We're investigating and recommend rotating the key. We can rotate for you if you want."
sec-bot: Action items recorded: [A1] Invalidate key cus_3hG7...zQp (raj) [A2] Rotate and provision new key for customer 8392 (infra) [A3] Fix frontend redaction bug (sam) [A4] Notify customer + CS runbook (toni) [A5] Run usage replay & create alert rules if abuse seen (maria).
raj: invalidation performed at 2026-03-20T09:28:10 UTC: `tokenctl revoke cus_3hG7...zQp --force`. New key not yet issued. Audit logs show no suspicious pattern beyond the three requests, but we'll run full replay.
maria: file a post-incident ticket with evidence and timeline. Also let's add an acceptance test to CI to ensure error reports never include keys.
sam: PR submitted to redact `extra.apiKey` and strip long-looking tokens from any text fields. will add unit tests.
toni: customer notified and accepted rotation; said no unexplained charges. CSM scheduled call for 09:45 UTC.
maria: follow-up: add a KMS-backed masking rule in the console that strips tokens by regex before they're forwarded to external services (Sentry). Can security/product ops scope this?
raj: agree. Will create RFC for masking via KMS envelope and update RBAC so only ops can change masking regex.
sec-bot: thread closed for now. Final status: key revoked, frontend fix PR opened, customer notified, replay running.
